title: Cap. VII §6: Effects compared — Pareus; reatus follows corruption; Sed pergamus
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles compares effects: what from Christ is not only inhering subjective righteousness but alien righteousness ours only by imputation; therefore what from Adam is not only inhering corruption but alien actual sin ours only by imputation. Placeus: no consequence without a bad omitted major. He grants moral+forensic righteousness from Christ opposed to corruption and following reatus, so moral+forensic injustice (corruption+reatus) from Adam — likeness that far. False that Christ's righteousness is ours only imputatively: it is gift accepted by faith (Apostle's gift-names; Pareus). Habitual/actual/passive readings of Christ's righteousness rebound badly onto Adam's side. Reatus following corruption is ours through that corruption, not imputation alone — denying this leaves Protestant confessions vs Pelagius/Pighius. A second reatus before corruption contradicts Garissoles p. 27 and makes God author of sin by judicial imputation. Sed pergamus.
pass_b_english: Next, he says, the effects of those causes are compared, namely sin and righteousness. What reaches us from Christ is not only inhering righteousness and ours subjectively, but also righteousness outside us, and another's, and ours only imputatively. Therefore what reaches us from Adam is not only inhering and habitual corruption, but also sin and disobedience outside us, and another's, and ours only by imputation. First there is no such consequence: for it rests on an omitted major proposition which, however conceived, will be — if universal — false; if particular — unfit to effect this conclusion. Next I confess that we have from Christ not only moral but also forensic righteousness, of which that is opposed to inhering corruption, this to the guilt which follows corruption; and so there has reached us from Adam not only moral but also forensic injustice, namely corruption and guilt. So far there is likeness. But D. Garissoles mixes in certain falsehoods. First it is false that Christ's righteousness is not ours except imputatively. For it is ours by the gift of God and of Christ, and also by our acceptance through faith. Therefore gift, donation by grace, overflow of grace, gift of righteousness is what the Apostle calls it. Who does not see that those names set a difference between the righteousness which reaches us from Christ and the sin which reaches us from Adam, in the mode by which they are ours? This gift is offered to us by the preaching of the Gospel and is received through faith. Therefore we are justified by faith. Pareus therefore speaks better: That the gift may be ours, it is received with a bought hand: so the gift of righteousness is ours when by faith we apply it to ourselves.

Next, which righteousness of Christ does he understand? Habitual? Then Adam's habitual injustice will have to be understood, not his actual sin. Actual of the whole life? Then likewise the actual injustice of Adam's whole life will have to be understood — which yet no one has said. The passive, as they call it, which in a moral sense is not righteousness but in a forensic? This is properly opposed only to guilt. But guilt is born from corruption. Therefore from Adam there reaches us a guilt following corruption, which is ours through that corruption, not through imputation only. Whoever denies this will depart from Scripture and from the doctrine of all the Protestant Churches, declared in confessions of faith and in disputations against Pelagius and Pighius. But if anyone not content with that says another guilt reaches us from Adam which precedes corruption and is ours only by imputation, he both posits two guilts — one before, one after corruption — contradicting D. Garissoles in places already noted by me at page 27 of this book, and will make God the author of our sin: inasmuch as by his judicial imputation he makes us sinners who otherwise would not be sinners: and, to be silent about the rest, will bring a new dogma into the Church beyond Scripture and the ancient faith. But let us go on.
source_text: Deinde, inquit, comparantur effecta illarum causarum, nimirum peccatum et iustitia. Quod a Christo ad nos pertingit, non est tantum iustitia inhaerens et nostra subiective, sed etiam iustitia extra nos, et aliena, et nostra nonnisi imputative. Ergo quod ab Adamo ad nos pertingit, non est tantum corruptio inhaerens et habitualis, sed etiam peccatum et inobedientia extra nos, et aliena, et nostra nonnisi per imputationem. Primum nulla est haec consequentia: nititur enim omissa propositione maiore, quae quocunque modo concipiatur, erit, si universalis, falsa; si particularis, inepta ad hanc efficiendam conclusionem. Deinde fateor nos a Christo non tantum moralem, sed etiam forensem iustitiam habere, quarum illa corruptioni inhaerenti, haec reatui, qui corruptionem sequitur, opponitur; itaque ab Adamo ad nos pertigisse non tantum moralem, sed etiam forensem iniustitiam, nempe corruptionem et reatum. Eatenus est similitudo. Sed admiscet D. G. falsa quaedam. Primo falsum est iustitiam Christi non esse nostram nisi imputative. Est enim nostra Dei et Christi dono, nec-non acceptione nostra per fidem. Itaque donum, donatio per gratiam, redundantia gratiae, donum iustitiae vocatur ab Apostolo. Quae nomina quis non videt discrimen ponere inter iustitiam quae a Christo, et peccatum quod ab Adamo ad nos pertingit, in modo quo sunt nostra? Offertur nobis hoc donum praedicatione Evangelii et accipitur per fidem. Itaque fide iustificamur. Melius igitur loquitur Pareus, Ut donum sit nostrum, empta manu accipitur: ita donum iustitiae nostrum sit, quando fide id nobis applicamus. Deinde quam Christi iustitiam intelligit? habitualem? habitualis igitur Adami iniustitia intelligenda erit, non autem eius peccatum actuale. Actualem totius vitae? Erit ergo similiter intelligenda actualis iniustitia totius vitae Adami, quod nemo tamen dixerit. Passivam quam vocant, quae morali quidem sensu iustitia non est, sed forensi? Haec proprie soli reatui opponitur. Nascitur autem ex corruptione reatus. Ab Adamo igitur ad nos pertingit reatus corruptionem sequens, qui per illam corruptionem noster est, non autem per imputationem tantum. Hoc qui negaverit, is a Scriptura et omnium Ecclesiarum protestantium doctrina, fidei confessionibus, et adversus Pelagium et Pighium disputationibus declarata discedet. Si quis autem eo non contentus alium dicat ab Adamo ad nos pertingere reatum, qui corruptionem antecedat, et noster non sit nisi per imputationem, is et duos reatus ponet, alterum priorem, alterum posteriorem corruptione, contradicente D. Garissolio locis iam a me notatis pag. huius lib. 27. et Deum faciet autorem peccati nostri: quippe qui iudiciaria sua imputatione peccatores nos facit, alioqui non peccatores: et, ut reliqua taceam, invehet novum dogma in Ecclesiam praeter Scripturam, et fidem antiquam. Sed pergamus.

choices.decision: Natural stop before Denique modus-effectorum; leave rest of Cap. VII for next densify
